record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one prove universality, both in the bulk and at every edge, for Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval?

evidence.quote: Another open problem in RMT is to prove universality, in the bulk and at (all) the edges, for Wigner ensembles in the case that the equilibrium measure for the ensemble is supported on more than one interval.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $W_N = (w_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le N}$ be a sequence of $N\times N$ real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) random matrices whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent (up to the symmetry constraint), have mean zero, and have variances $\sigma_{ij}^2 = \mathbb{E}|w_{ij}|^2$ chosen so that the empirical spectral measure of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$ converges weakly almost surely to a deterministic compactly supported probability measure $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ (the equilibrium / self-consistent density of states), and such that higher moments of the entries satisfy standard sub-exponential tail bounds. Assume that the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a finite disjoint union of more than one interval, i.e.\ 
$$\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}) = \bigcup_{k=1}^{p}[a_k,b_k], \qquad p\ge 2, \qquad b_k<a_{k+1}.$$

Prove the following local spectral universality statements for the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\le\dots\le\lambda_N$ of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$:

(a) (Bulk universality.) For every $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ and every fixed $k\ge 1$, the rescaled $k$-point correlation function of the eigenvalues near $E$ converges, as $N\to\infty$, to the corresponding sine-kernel determinantal/Pfaffian correlation function of the GUE (in the complex Hermitian case) or GOE (in the real symmetric case).

(b) (Edge universality at every edge.) For each $k\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ and at both endpoints $a_k$ and $b_k$ of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ — including the internal edges $b_1,a_2,b_2,\dots,a_p$ as well as the two external edges $a_1$ and $b_p$ — the appropriately rescaled extremal eigenvalues of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$ near that edge converge in distribution to the Tracy–Widom law of the corresponding symmetry class (TW$_2$ in the complex Hermitian case, TW$_1$ in the real symmetric case).
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: for general correlated Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval (multi-cut) self-consistent density of states, Alt–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder established edge universality at internal edges (band rigidity and Tracy–Widom limits), and bulk universality results are available in many correlated/Wigner-type settings. Cusp universality has also been established. However, the problem as originally posed for general Wigner ensembles with multi-cut equilibrium measure (covering both bulk and all edges in full generality) is regarded as substantially advanced but not uniformly settled in all symmetry classes and generality; recent literature treats it as partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Correlated Random Matrices: Band Rigidity and Edge Universality
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem applies to internal edges of the self-consistent density of states; establishes band rigidity and edge universality.
status_evidence.claim: Edge universality at internal edges of multi-cut self-consistent density of states is established for correlated Wigner-type matrices.

status_evidence.title: Cusp Universality for Correlated Random Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Cusp universality established for correlated random matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Cusp universality (transition between multi-cut regimes) has been proved, contributing to multi-interval universality.

status_evidence.title: Edge Universality for Deformed Wigner Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy-Widom limit established for deformed Wigner H=W+V whose density may have multiple components.
status_evidence.claim: Edge universality for deformed Wigner ensembles, a class with potentially multi-interval equilibrium measure.
